title: Unary Signs, Parentheses, and Recursive Progress

blocks.text: A Unit Can Contain Another Expression

A term now combines units. A unit can be a number, a + sign followed by another unit, a - sign followed by another unit, or an expression enclosed in ( and ). The outer expression retains addition and subtraction of terms, and each term retains multiplication and division of units. This grammar allows -(4+3)*2; without changing token recognition.

A binary sign relates two operands: 8-3. A unary sign applies to a single unit: -3. The - token is the same; the rule receiving it decides its role. After * or /, the right-hand unit can also begin with a unary sign, as in 8/-2.

Parentheses allow a unit to request a complete expression. The reader consumes ( before that call and requires ) afterward. The inner expression returns the closing token because it does not belong to its loop; the unit that opened the grouping is responsible for consuming it.

blocks.question: Which responsibility belongs to the unit rule when accepting (3+4)?
options: Consume the opening parenthesis, request the inner expression, and check and consume its closing parenthesis.
Skip both parentheses without checking and combine all signs in one loop.
Return ( as though it were a number with value 0.
blocks.explanation: The rule that opens the group must validate its closing delimiter. The expression level may stop when it encounters ), but cannot by itself decide that the grouping is complete.

leer_unidad can call leer_expresion, and through terms leer_expresion can request another unit. Recall placing a function declaration before its definition: declare the signature of leer_expresion before defining leer_unidad. Do not duplicate its implementation or bypass the compiler's checks.

This fragment is integrated after the reader and resultado_en_dominio. profundidad counts nested opening parentheses and unary signs, starting at 0. Only those recursive steps increment it. Levels up to 8 are accepted; requesting a level greater than 8 rejects the input before proceeding.

Every recursive branch has already consumed +, -, or ( before making its call. A number terminates the unit without further recursion. An unexpected token is preserved so that a diagnostic or later recovery policy can observe its boundary. Negating a value in -100..100 is safe and preserves that domain; we do not negate arbitrary values outside that contract.

blocks.explanation: The grouped unit obtains 7 from its inner expression and consumes ). The outer term uses that unit in a multiplication by 3.

blocks.explanation: The unit produces -9. Integer division by 2 truncates toward zero and produces -4; the outer addition adds 3 and produces -1.

blocks.text: Guided Integration of Unary Signs and Grouping

This guided integration brings together the preceding fragments: connect their declarations and definitions to the program, preserve their signatures, and check progress and limits. The editor starts with the terms stage without grouping. Extend it to accept numeric units, unary + and - signs, and parenthesized expressions. For "-(4+3)*2;", it must produce Result: -14. Pass an initial depth of 0 and increment it only when entering after a unary sign or opening parenthesis. A level greater than 8 must be rejected as excessive nesting.

Keep numeric literals in 0..99, intermediate results in -100..100, input text at most 64 ASCII characters, checked division, and a single operation terminated by ;. "2*(3+4);" gives 14; "-9/2;" and "8/-2;" give -4; "+5;" gives 5; "--6;" gives 6. Reject "8/(3-3);" before dividing. "(2+3;" is missing a closing parenthesis, and "2(3+4);" is missing a binary sign: implicit multiplication is not supported.

Test eight + signs followed by 1 and ;: the result must be 1. Nine + signs followed by 1 and ; must be rejected for nesting depth. Also check result boundaries with "99+1;" and "-99-1;", which yield 100 and -100. "100;" remains a literal outside the domain: the ranges for literals and results differ.

Choose the necessary declaration, the location of each return, and the level that consumes each closing parenthesis. Before running, justify which unit was consumed before each recursive call. The editor does not validate those limits or the grammar automatically; compare the tests and check that the extension preserves prior addition, subtraction, precedence, and associativity.
Compare the Integration After Building It

This reference uses "-(3+2)*(4-1);" and produces -15. The token interface remains stable: the grammar uses the units already recognized and returns those belonging to another level. The expression declaration lets a grouped unit call it before its definition.

Compare the contract and tests with your version. Eight unary signs reach depth 8 and permit reading the number; a ninth would request depth 9 and is rejected. The check does not replace progress: signs are consumed before the calls. Term and expression functions pass along the level without incrementing it for each binary calculation.

blocks.text: An Observable Call Does Not Prove Termination

blocks.question: A version returns the same ( it just obtained and calls the expression again without consuming it or increasing a limit. What is wrong?
options: Only value validation is missing: the finite text length already guarantees termination.
The new traversal can encounter the same opening parenthesis again without making progress.
Only the closing delimiter needs checking: returning the opening parenthesis already ensures the next call advances.
blocks.explanation: Recursion must advance or reduce the problem. Finite input does not guarantee termination if a rule keeps asking about the same unit. Returning the opening parenthesis leaves it available; repeating the same question without consuming it can reproduce the same state indefinitely.

blocks.text: A termination argument combines the returning case, consumption before each recursive call, and the depth limit. Here the representations have finite length and every accepted opening parenthesis or unary sign is consumed. Finishing a grouping also consumes the closing delimiter; no remaining call should reinterpret it as a new unit.
Prepare Diagnostics and Recovery by Operation

The grammar now distinguishes units, terms, and expressions. The application still abandons the entire attempt upon catching the first error. For a small interpreter with several operations, we will change the outer level: it will display the diagnostic, consume input up to that operation's end, and continue without losing the following one. The semicolon must be preserved if a rule obtained it while discovering a missing operand. The grouping and unary-sign rules adapt the supporting reading (Stroustrup, 2024, sections 5.5.4 and 6.4). The depth limit, preservation of unexpected boundaries, and activities are original to this learning path.
